title: Chapter 12 — The Price of the Mark

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The first real cost arrived two days after the warning note.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They had been working a narrow cut behind the tanners' row—two notches of their own, no forged third, nothing that should have drawn attention. The passage was short and already starting to close when BAH-lahg's spear found something soft under the dust at the far end.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It was a pack. Ordinary. Canvas and leather, the kind any lower-district porter carried. The straps had been cut clean through. Inside was a water skin, a half-eaten loaf gone hard, and a small clay tablet wrapped in cloth. No name. No identifying marks. Just the ordinary gear of someone who had expected to walk out again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun unwrapped the tablet. The writing was hurried and already fading at the edges, as if the clay itself had decided the words were temporary.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: THE CITY DOES NOT LIKE WITNESSES
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: I SHOULD NOT HAVE FOLLOWED THE MARKS
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: So we're not the only ones.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: We were never the only ones,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun said. Her voice had gone flat.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: We were just the ones still walking.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg turned the empty pack over with the butt of his spear.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: No blood. No body. Just the gear.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek crouched beside the pack instead of answering immediately.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The canvas had rotted at the corners but not enough to explain its condition. One strap had been sliced cleanly through. The other looked as though someone had started to cut it before changing their mind.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: How long has this passage been here?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun looked up from the tablet.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Or recently enough that the city hasn't decided otherwise.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek searched the pack more carefully.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Two fishing hooks wrapped in cloth.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then his fingers touched something hidden inside the lining.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He carefully split the loose stitching.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A tiny clay token fell into his palm.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: So somebody expected to come back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at the carefully hidden token.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He folded the lining back into place.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They took the tablet. They left the pack where it was. On the way out Ninsun cut a fourth notch beside their original two—deeper, angrier, the kind of mark that said this place had already collected its price. Zeek didn't stop her.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That night the cheap room felt smaller.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg leaned his spear against the wall but kept looking toward the door as though expecting another messenger to appear.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo poured water into four cups.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The fourth sat untouched beside the abandoned pack.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: After several minutes BAH-lahg pointed at it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She hadn't realized she'd poured it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Without answering, she emptied the cup back into the jar.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I'm trying to remember every name I've ever found scratched out.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: What if one of them belonged to him?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: You don't know it was a man.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: What if he never found a shifted street?

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You think he was like us.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Someone else might have reached exactly the same conclusions.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: And disappeared before leaving more than three hurried lines.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun sat on the floor with her map spread wide, the warning note, the uncrossed name, and the new tablet arranged in a careful line beside it. She had drawn a second box around the tanners' row and written a single word inside:

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg cleaned his spear in silence. En-HEH-doo turned the small copper figurine between her fingers and said nothing. Zeek sat with his back against the wall and did not open the journal. Six days now. The decision still felt like the only clean thing he owned in this place.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: After a long time En-HEH-doo spoke.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: We keep marking, someone else pays. We stop marking, we walk blind. That's the math.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Same fucking math as always. Just higher numbers.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun didn't look up from the map.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He flexed his left hand inside the linen. The mark was warm. Not demanding. Just present, like a second pulse that had decided it belonged there.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Outside, the lower districts continued their ordinary noise—arguments, animals, the constant low pressure of a city that never fully slept. Somewhere in those streets another passage was probably opening. Or closing. Or waiting for the next set of marks to decide whether the people who cut them would be allowed to walk back out.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Now someone else had paid the first real price for it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek lay against the wall with the journal still sealed inside his pack.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Every hour he refused to open it felt like a choice he had made himself.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Every shifted street made that choice feel smaller.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Somewhere beneath the city, another explorer had vanished badly enough to leave his food behind, his water unfinished, and his warning still waiting to be read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek wondered how many others had done the same.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He wondered how many maps had been started.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: How many journals had remained closed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: How many people had believed they were discovering the First City.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Outside, somewhere below the ordinary streets of Uruk, stone answered stone with a single distant knock.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This time, nobody in the room pretended they hadn't heard it.
